chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The habitual drinker of wine is like an idol worshipper. When he dies while being habitual over it, he will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when he meets Him, like an idol worshipper.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a habitual wine drinker according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the gravity of chronic intoxication by equating the spiritual state of a habitual wine drinker with that of an idol worshipper, reflecting the Shia juristic view that persistent sin alters one's ontological standing before God. It highlights the concept of 'dying upon the habit,' where the continuous practice of drinking solidifies a state akin to shirk in the eyes of Allah, serving as a severe warning for those who do not repent before death.
